gap_slide.heading: Level 5 — The gap Stack Internal fills
gap_slide.subheading: The knowledge substrate underneath an AI-native bank

rows.title: Ground the agents
rows.desc: Agentic AI and conversational banking are only as good as the knowledge they retrieve. Stack Internal provides the curated, current, human-validated layer — with provenance — that generic document stores can't.

rows.title: Close the loop on AI-written code
rows.desc: 40% AI-written code means engineering knowledge decays fast unless capture is built into the workflow. The closed loop — ask, answer, validate, reuse — turns 17,000 agentic developers into a compounding asset, via MCP write-back rather than read-only retrieval.

rows.title: Model-agnostic by design
rows.desc: Their architecture is deliberately modular and vendor-neutral. We are not competing with the OpenAI partnership — we're the knowledge layer every model in their ecosystem draws from.

rows.title: Governance they can defend
rows.desc: Responsible AI is a mandatory training module and a regulatory reality. Attribution, SME validation and Content Health give auditable answers to “why did the agent say that?”

gap_slide.positioning_line: “You've committed €1bn of value to AI. We make sure the knowledge it runs on is worth trusting.”
gap_slide.notes: Lead with grounding agents and the closed loop; keep the model-vendor point defensive-ready, not defensive-sounding.

objections_slide.heading: Likely objections — and how to handle them
objections_slide.subheading: INTERNAL — not for sharing with the account

objections.objection: We're all-in on OpenAI and Microsoft. We want fewer tools, not more — why add another platform to the stack?
objections.counter_anchor: You've said your architecture is deliberately modular and vendor-neutral.
objections.counter: Stack Internal isn't a model or a copilot — it's the knowledge layer every model in your ecosystem retrieves from. Adding it doesn't expand the vendor footprint; it improves the fidelity of everything already in it.

objections.objection: We already have SharePoint and internal wikis. Our people know where to find things.
objections.counter_anchor: 40% of your code is now written by AI agents, not people.
objections.counter: When agents are the consumers, people knowing where to find things stops being the measure. The question is whether knowledge is structured, validated, and retrievable by a machine with provenance — and whether it's being captured as it's created.

objections.objection: We have 6,000+ developers and strong AI capability internally. We could build something like this.
objections.counter_anchor: You've committed €1bn to AI business value in three years.
objections.counter: Building a knowledge platform is a multi-year product problem, not an AI problem. Every month that engineering knowledge isn't being captured and validated is decay you can't get back. The opportunity cost is measured in the productivity gains you've already published.

objections.objection: We have strict controls on where data lives. We can't have sensitive IP going to a third party.
objections.counter_anchor: Your Responsible AI module is now mandatory for all 185,000 employees.
objections.counter: Stack Internal holds engineering and institutional knowledge — not customer data. Attribution, SME validation, and Content Health give you the audit trail your Responsible AI policy requires. We can deploy in your environment with no external data movement.

objections.objection: We've just rolled out AI tools to the entire workforce. Change fatigue is real — we can't ask people to adopt another new thing.
objections.counter_anchor: The closed loop works inside the tools your developers are already using.
objections.counter: Stack Internal integrates via MCP into the agentic coding environment your 17,000 developers are already in. The ask is ask-and-validate here rather than learn a new product — it surfaces at the moment of work, not as a separate destination.

objections_slide.notes: Lead with the vendor consolidation counter — it's the most common opening objection in a bank with a named AI partner. Handle the security objection before the demo, not during it. Never argue against the incumbent knowledge store directly — redirect to what the agents retrieve from.

entry_slide.heading: Entry points and next moves

cards.title: Who to reach
cards.desc: Chief Data & AI Officer organisation (Ricardo Martín Manjón) owns the €1bn value target. Group COO/CTO Juan Olaizola owns the 2026–27 technology strategy. Developer tooling and platform engineering under Gravity are the practitioner door.

cards.title: The UK angle
cards.desc: Santander UK just completed the TSB acquisition — a major integration with heavy engineering knowledge-transfer risk. Integration programmes are acute, time-boxed knowledge problems: a natural first conversation for a UK-based team.

cards.title: Discovery questions
cards.desc: Where does validated engineering knowledge live for your 17,000 agentic developers? What grounds your agents' answers today, and can you show provenance? How is TSB integration knowledge being captured before it walks?

cards.title: Next moves
cards.desc: Build the contact map against the CD&AI and platform orgs. Line up the closed-loop / MCP write-back demo as the stakeholder-access vehicle. Track quarterly AI value announcements as timing triggers.
